title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Chronic Pain
recommendation_text: Use the 'Universal Precautions' approach with these specific questions: 1) 'How many doses of pain medication have you missed in the past week?' 2) 'Have you ever taken more medication than prescribed when your pain was worse?' 3) 'Have you ever used someone else's medication for your pain?' 4) 'Have you ever obtained pain medication from more than one provider?' Document responses without judgment.
implementation_guidance: Implement at initiation of therapy and at each refill visit. Use a matter-of-fact, non-accusatory tone. Document responses verbatim. Develop clear protocols for addressing concerning responses, including referral to pain specialists or addiction services when appropriate.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of medication misuse patterns, 15-20% reduction in aberrant medication behaviors, and more appropriate pain management referrals.
target_population: Patients on long-term opioid therapy for chronic pain
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with significant potential for reducing opioid-related complications and healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Gourlay DL, Heit HA, Almahrezi A
citation_title: Universal precautions in pain medicine: a rational approach to the treatment of chronic pain

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Depression
recommendation_text: Implement the 'Side Effect Management Protocol': 1) Ask 'What side effects are you experiencing from your medication?' 2) Rate each side effect on a scale of 1-10 for severity 3) For side effects rated >5, implement specific management strategies (e.g., taking medication with food for GI effects, timing doses earlier for insomnia) 4) Document side effects and management plan.
implementation_guidance: Implement at 1-2 weeks after starting antidepressants and at each follow-up visit. Create a side effect management handout with common strategies. Schedule more frequent follow-up for patients with significant side effects.
expected_outcomes: 30-40% reduction in medication discontinuation due to side effects, 25-30% improvement in overall adherence rates, and improved depression treatment outcomes.
target_population: Patients starting or currently taking antidepressant medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for improving depression outcomes and reducing healthcare utilization.
citation_title: Tolerability and adherence issues in antidepressant therapy

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Older Adults with Polypharmacy
recommendation_text: Conduct a 'Medication Timing Assessment' by asking: 1) 'Walk me through your typical day and tell me exactly when you take each medication' 2) 'What system do you use to remember which medications to take and when?' 3) 'What challenges do you face with your medication schedule?' 4) 'How do you adjust your medication schedule when your routine changes?' Document responses and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Use visual aids like medication timing charts. Implement during comprehensive medication reviews. Document specific timing issues identified and interventions implemented. Consider medication consolidation to reduce dosing frequency when appropriate.
expected_outcomes: Identification of timing-related adherence issues in 40-50% of older adults with polypharmacy, 20-25% improvement in medication adherence rates, and reduced adverse drug events.
target_population: Older adults taking 5 or more medications daily
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with significant potential for reducing medication-related hospitalizations and adverse events.
citation_authors: Conn VS, Hafdahl AR, Cooper PS, et al.
citation_title: Interventions to improve medication adherence among older adults: meta-analysis of adherence outcomes among randomized controlled trials

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in COPD
recommendation_text: Ask patients with COPD these specific questions about inhaler use: 1) 'How many times in the past week did you miss using your maintenance inhaler?' 2) 'What time of day do you use your maintenance inhaler?' 3) 'How do you know when to use your rescue inhaler versus your maintenance inhaler?' 4) 'Can you show me how you use each of your inhalers?' Document responses and correct technique errors.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Keep placebo inhalers for demonstration. Document specific technique errors observed and corrections provided. Consider spacer devices for patients with coordination issues.
expected_outcomes: Identification of technique errors in 60-70% of patients, 25-30% improvement in inhaler technique, and reduced COPD exacerbations.
target_population: Patients with COPD using multiple inhalers
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing emergency department visits and hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Sanchis J, Gich I, Pedersen S
citation_title: Systematic Review of Errors in Inhaler Use: Has Patient Technique Improved Over Time?

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Glaucoma
recommendation_text: Implement the 'Glaucoma Medication Adherence Technique' (G-MAT): 1) Assess technique - observe patient instilling drops 2) Identify barriers - ask about specific challenges 3) Provide solutions - offer targeted interventions (e.g., drop guides, alarms) 4) Demonstrate - show proper technique 5) Practice - have patient demonstrate back. Document interventions implemented.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Keep artificial tears for technique practice. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Consider auto-drop devices for patients with dexterity issues.
expected_outcomes: 30-40% improvement in eye drop instillation technique, 20-25% improvement in adherence rates, and better intraocular pressure control.
target_population: Patients with glaucoma on topical medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for preventing disease progression and vision loss.
citation_authors: Sleath B, Blalock SJ, Carpenter DM, et al.
citation_title: Provider education about glaucoma and glaucoma medications during videotaped medical visits

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Transplant Recipients
recommendation_text: Use the 'BATHE' technique during medication reviews: B (Background) - 'How have things been going with your medications?' A (Affect) - 'How do you feel about taking these medications long-term?' T (Trouble) - 'What troubles you most about your medication regimen?' H (Handling) - 'How are you handling these challenges?' E (Empathy) - Express understanding and validate concerns. Document responses and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement at each follow-up visit. Create a standardized documentation template. Develop clear protocols for addressing identified adherence barriers. Consider electronic monitoring for high-risk patients.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of psychosocial barriers to adherence, 25-30% improvement in immunosuppressant adherence rates, and reduced rejection episodes.
target_population: Solid organ transplant recipients on immunosuppressive medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for preventing costly rejection episodes and graft failure.
citation_authors: De Geest S, Dobbels F, Fluri C, et al.
citation_title: Adherence to the therapeutic regimen in heart, lung, and heart-lung transplant recipients

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
recommendation_text: Ask patients with IBD these specific questions about maintenance medications: 1) 'In the past month, how many days did you miss taking your IBD medication?' 2) 'What makes it difficult to take your medication regularly?' 3) 'Do you ever skip doses when you're feeling well?' 4) 'What concerns do you have about long-term use of these medications?' Document responses and provide targeted education.
implementation_guidance: Implement during routine follow-up visits. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific misconceptions identified and education provided. Emphasize the importance of continuous therapy even during symptom-free periods.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient understanding of maintenance therapy, 20-25% improvement in adherence rates, and reduced disease flares.
target_population: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease on maintenance therapy
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing hospitalizations and complications.
citation_authors: Jackson CA, Clatworthy J, Robinson A, et al.
citation_title: Factors associated with non-adherence to oral medication for inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Diabetes
recommendation_text: Implement the 'SIMPLE' approach for diabetes medication adherence: S (Simplify) - reduce dosing frequency when possible; I (Impart) - explain how each medication works; M (Modify) - address beliefs about medications; P (Provide) - offer adherence tools; L (Listen) - elicit and address concerns; E (Evaluate) - assess adherence at each visit. Document interventions used.
implementation_guidance: Create a checklist to ensure all components are addressed. Implement at initiation of therapy and reinforce at follow-up visits. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented.
expected_outcomes: 25-30% improvement in diabetes medication adherence rates, 0.5-0.8% reduction in HbA1c levels, and reduced diabetes-related complications.
target_population: Patients with diabetes on oral medications or insulin
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for reducing diabetes-related hospitalizations and complications.
citation_authors: Capoccia K, Odegard PS, Letassy N
citation_title: Medication Adherence With Diabetes Medication: A Systematic Review of the Literature

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Medication Adherence in Parkinson's Disease
recommendation_text: Use the 'Timing Matters' assessment by asking: 1) 'How often do you take your Parkinson's medication exactly as prescribed?' 2) 'Do you ever delay or skip doses because of side effects?' 3) 'Do you notice your symptoms returning before your next scheduled dose?' 4) 'What system do you use to remember your medication times?' Document responses and implement targeted interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication reviews. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific adherence patterns and motor fluctuations. Consider medication timing adjustments or extended-release formulations for patients with wearing-off symptoms.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of suboptimal medication timing, 20-30% reduction in off-time, and improved quality of life scores.
target_population: Patients with Parkinson's disease on dopaminergic medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for improving symptom control and quality of life.
citation_title: Effect of educational intervention on medication timing in Parkinson's disease: a randomized controlled trial

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Adherence in Osteoporosis
recommendation_text: Ask patients on osteoporosis medications these specific questions: 1) 'What time of day do you take your bone medication?' 2) 'How long do you wait before eating or lying down after taking it?' 3) 'How often do you miss doses?' 4) 'What side effects have you experienced?' Document responses and provide targeted education to address misconceptions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication reviews. Use a non-judgmental approach. Document specific adherence patterns and barriers. Provide written instructions for proper administration of bisphosphonates.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of administration errors, 20-25% improvement in adherence rates, and better bone mineral density outcomes.
target_population: Patients on oral bisphosphonates or other osteoporosis medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential for preventing fractures and associated costs.
citation_authors: Kothawala P, Badamgarav E, Ryu S, et al.
citation_title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of real-world adherence to drug therapy for osteoporosis
